commands.summary: Create a song and open it: Mixer 1 "Sources", Mixer 2 "Buses" with the bus "Main" → master, and the output port "Main" (R-MIX-3). --template <name>: the template's song instead (R-PRESET-2) — its tempo, meter and rate unless --bpm, --sig, --rate say; yours of a name before the factory's.
Open a song. If it has an autosave newer than it (unsaved edits from a session that never saved), says `recovery: …` and the model's `recovery` names it (R-SAFE-2).
Write the .slp (a path saves it there).
Close the song and return Home (its autosave is dropped: closing is choosing).
Open the song from its autosave (`<path>.autosave`, written while it had unsaved edits — R-SAFE-1): the song as it was, unsaved, saved to <path> by `project save`.
Delete a song's autosave — the saved song is the one kept.

Write addresses: project.bpm, <strip>.gain, <clip>.at, <device>.<param> (any DSP registry parameter, in its unit), … — `api` lists every one. An unknown address or parameter is refused. A value starting with `=` is a FORMULA that drives a number (R-AUTO); a plain number clears it.
Print an address's stored value.

Undo the last edit (prints what): back to the history node's parent. Consecutive `set`s of the same addresses — a fader dragged — are ONE step. A machine setting, the transport and a save are not edits; a new or opened song starts a new history.
Redo: forward to the NEWEST branch below the current node (prints what). An edit after an undo no longer clears it — it starts another branch, and the old ones stay (R-HIST-1).
The song's history as a tree: one node a line — `*` at the current one, its id, its parent's (`-` at the root), what made it. --json: the same as `history[]` in the model.
Make history node <id> the song (prints what made it) — as undo does, it moves through the tree and is no node itself; the song is unsaved and the player hears it.
Add a mixer page after the last one.
Delete an empty mixer. Refused while strips live on it.
Move a mixer to position <index> (0 = first). Refused if it would make any route point backward.

Add a strip. Default mixer: the first for audio/instrument, the second for a bus; default output: "Main" — the bus that leaves the nearest later mixer with buses, else the one leaving its own mixer (the new strip is then placed BEFORE it, so the route goes forward), else master. An instrument strip gets its instrument (default synth) as its first device; --sample <file> gives a sampler its sound (R-EDM-8); --plugin <id|name> makes it another maker's instrument plugin, from `plugins list` (R-VST-6).
Delete a strip and its rack. Refused while clips play through it or strips route to it, unless --with-clips (its clips go too).

Move a strip to another mixer (at its end) and/or to position --order <n> on it (0 = first); its mixer's strips renumber in their new order, as `mixer move` renumbers mixers. Refused if a route would point backward.

Render a strip's OWN sound — its clips or notes through its instrument and rack, at unity, before its fader, to the song's end and its tail — beside the song (Frozen/<strip> <id>.wav, 32-bit float) and play that instead: its clips, notes and devices kept but idle; its fader, pan, sends and output as ever. Only a strip nothing feeds; the song saved (R-PERF-3).
Play a frozen strip's own work again (the file stays) (R-PERF-3).
Render a strip's own sound as a freeze does (Bounces/<strip> <n>.wav) and put it as an audio clip at beat 0 on a NEW strip; the strip itself untouched. Prints the clip, then `made:` (R-PERF-3).
Move EVERY clip playing through <ch> to strip --to, one edit. Refused across kinds: audio clips need an audio strip, note clips an instrument strip; a bus plays no clips.

Arm an instrument strip for the MIDI keyboard (R-MIDI-2): what is played sounds through it at once — through the song while it plays, through an input monitor (the song's mix without its clips) while stopped — the sustain pedal held; `none` disarms. Not an edit: the song does not keep it. Opens the MIDI inputs `settings midiInputs` names. Or arm an AUDIO line for its input (R-REC-1): heard through it as `<ch>.monitor` says, recorded by `transport record`; --input <port> sets its input first (that part an edit).

A logical port (R-DEV-3): an output the master or a strip can feed, or an INPUT (--dir in) an audio line records (R-REC-1); this machine's settings say which device it is (`settings set port.<name>=<device>`). Prints its id.

A side-chain in one line: a Compressor at the end of <ch>'s rack, its Sidechain on, keyed by a pre-fader sidechain send from --under — attack 1 ms, release half a beat, threshold −30 dB and the ratio that makes a full-scale key cut --amount dB (default 8, 1 … 24). The key must come EARLIER in processing order (R-MIX-4). One edit, one undo; prints the compressor, then `made:`.
Set a strip's main output: a strip LATER in processing order (a later mixer, or after it on its own), master, or an output port.

Add a send (post-fader unless --pre). Same forward-only rule as `route`. With --sidechain it is a KEY: it feeds the target's compressors' detectors (their Sidechain switch), not its input, and goes to a strip (R-MIX-15).
Remove a send.

Insert a DSP registry device into a rack (default: at the end). An instrument goes only first on an instrument strip. --plugin <id|name> (instead of --type) inserts another maker's effect plugin, from `plugins list`: it plays in a process of its own, its parameters are p<id>, numbers 0 … 1 (R-VST-6). --sample <file> gives a device that plays a recording its file in the same line — a convolution reverb's impulse response (R-FX-14); `<dv>.sample` changes it after.
Remove a device from its rack. An instrument strip keeps its instrument.
Move a device within its rack.
Add a timeline lane at the bottom. With --strip <instrument>: that instrument's TRACK — what is put on it plays through it, and it shows the strip's name until given its own (R-LANE-3).
Delete a lane. Refused while clips are drawn on it, unless --with-clips.

Move a lane to row <index> (0 = the top); the lanes renumber in their new order. A lane moved out of its group's run leaves it, one moved into another group's run joins it; a group (lg_n) moves whole, its first lane to <index> (R-ARR-3).

Gather lanes into a NEW named group (R-ARR-3): side by side at the first one's place, in their order; a lane already in another group leaves it. Folded (`set <lg>.folded=on`) the group is one row showing all its clips. Prints its id.
Let a group's lanes go; the group is gone, the lanes stay where they are.

Place a clip. With --src: an audio clip; a file the song has not used gets its own new strip on the first mixer (R-MIX-2), a used one reuses its strip. With --strip <instrument>: a note clip of --pattern (a new empty 4-beat pattern if none). With --instrument <type>: the same on a NEW instrument strip of that type — what dropping an instrument does (R-BROWSE-3); --plugin <id|name> the same with another maker's instrument plugin (R-VST-6). With no --lane it goes on the lane its strip's clips are on (the newest one's), a new lane only for a strip with none; --lane new asks for a new one (R-SVC-8). On an instrument's TRACK (--lane <ln>) a note clip plays through that instrument — --strip may be left out, --pattern places that pattern; audio and --instrument are refused there (R-LANE-3). --warp (with --src): it follows the song's tempo, its own detected now (R-WARP-1; refused when none is heard). Prints the clip, then `made:` and whatever else it made.

Move a clip in time, to another lane (where it is drawn), and/or another strip (what it sounds through). Onto an instrument's TRACK a note clip is re-routed to that instrument (and says so); a clip on a track told --strip <another> goes to that one's track; audio is refused on a track (R-LANE-3).

A copy right after it (or at --at); --count N makes N copies end to end; --lane puts them on another lane (onto an instrument's TRACK a note clip's copy plays through that instrument; audio is refused there, as a move is — R-CLIP-8). A note clip's copy plays the SAME pattern — linked. Prints the first copy, then `made:` the rest. Shift-drag and Ctrl+V in the window are this line (R-CLIP-9/10).
Give a note clip its own copy of its pattern.
Remove a clip.
Create an empty pattern.

Add a note to a pattern — every clip of it changes. A pitch is a number, a name (C4 = 60, F#3, Bb2) or a kit's pad (kick). --chord <Cm7> adds a chord instead (its root in --octave, default 4; --inversion n raises its n lowest notes an octave) as ONE edit — the qualities are under Notation. --chance: the odds it sounds in a pass (1). A pattern locked to a scale (`pattern scale`) puts each note on the scale's nearest pitch, a tie down — a major chord on any degree becomes that degree's own triad.
Remove the note at that pitch and time.

Hear one note through instrument strip <ch> — its instrument and its rack, at its fader and pan, as it sounds in the song — on a stream of its own, whether the song plays or not (the piano roll's sound when a note is made, a key pressed). A pitch is a number, a name or the strip's kit's pad; --length beats (default 0.5), --vel (default 100). A preview started while one rings takes over with a short fade. Not an edit, never in a render.

Change the note at --pitch / --at: move it (--to-pitch, --to-at), resize it (--length), set its velocity (--vel) or its chance (--chance) — one gesture, one line. Refused onto another note. In a pattern locked to a scale, --to-pitch goes on to the scale's next pitch the way it moved.

Move every note's start onto the grid (default a sixteenth, 0.25), delaying every second grid step by --swing of a step — or onto a --groove (R-ROLL-11: a template's steps, offsets and accents, under Notation; it carries its own grid and swing). --strength moves each start (and velocity) that part of the way (1). --notes: only those notes (the roll's selection). Notes that land on one another merge (the louder stays).

Move several clips in time as ONE edit (R-ARR-3 — a folded group's clips dragged together; any selection): each --by beats (negative = earlier). Refused whole, naming the first, when a clip is not the song's or would start before beat 0.

Many notes in ONE edit (one undo step): each <note> is <pitch>@<beat>[:<length>[:<vel>[:<chance>]]] — C4@0:0.5:90, kick@1, E4@2::70, hat@1.5:::0.5. --length / --vel are the defaults (0.25, 100). A bad token is refused by name and nothing lands. Prints how many. A note past the pattern's end grows the pattern to the end of that bar, and a clip that played it whole with it (R-ROLL-9). A scale-locked pattern puts each on its scale (R-ROLL-11).

Move several notes as ONE edit (one undo step) — the piano roll's selection dragged, or moved by the arrow keys: each named by <pitch>@<beat>, all moved --by beats (default 0) and --semi semitones (default 0). Refused whole, naming the first, when a name matches no note, or a note would land on one not moved, below beat 0 or outside 0–127.
Remove several notes as ONE edit — the piano roll's selection deleted. Refused whole, naming the first, when a name matches no note.

A step row: x = a note, X = an accent (velocity 127), . or - = a rest, one per --step (default 0.25) from --at (default 0); spaces and | are ignored. REPLACES that pitch's notes in the span; --length defaults to a step. One edit.
A new pattern with the same notes and length (named "<name> copy"). Prints its id.
Remove every note (or only --pitch's).
Delete a pattern. Refused while a clip plays it (naming the clips).

A point on one of a pattern's expression lanes (R-MIDI-3): the pitch wheel (`bend`, −1 … +1) or a controller (`cc0` … `cc127`, 0 … 1; `mod` is `cc1`) — linear to the next point, held before the first and after the last; a point already at that beat is moved to the value. The instruments play `bend` and `cc1` (their wheels); every lane goes out in a MIDI file.
Remove the lane's point at --at.
Remove a lane's points (--lane), or every lane's.

A named place in the song (R-ARR-1 — Interstellar's marker, in beats): with --length a SECTION, else a point whose section runs to the next marker (or the song's end). On the ruler; `transport seek <mk>` goes there, `transport loop <mk>` loops its section. Prints its id.
Rename a marker (and set its --note).
Move a marker (--at) and/or set its section's --length (0: a point again).
Delete a marker.

Change the song's tempo (R-TEMPO-1): --bpm from --at (beats after 0; the start's tempo is `project.bpm`) on — or, with --ramp, reached there gliding from the tempo before. Every beat-to-time conversion follows the map: the render, playback, the metronome, recording, warped clips, the MIDI file. Prints its id.
Move a tempo change (--at), change its --bpm, or whether it is reached gliding (--ramp true|false).
Delete a tempo change: the tempo before it holds on.
Save a device's set values (and a sampler's sound) as a preset of its type in your presets folder (R-PRESET-1) — a name you have is refused without --replace. The machine's, not the song's: no undo.

Set a device to a preset of its type — every value back to its default, then the preset's, ONE edit; yours of a name before the factory's (R-PRESET-1). `device add --preset` and `clip add --instrument --preset` drop one in.
The presets, yours and the factory's, by type (R-PRESET-1).

Keep the open song as a template in your templates folder (R-PRESET-2) — as it is, every file it names made absolute; a name you have refused without --replace. The machine's, not the song's: no undo. `project new <path> --template <name>` starts a song from it.
The song templates, yours and the factory's (R-PRESET-2).
Delete a template of yours (a factory's is refused) — no undo (R-PRESET-2).
Delete a preset of yours (a factory's is refused) — the machine's, no undo (R-PRESET-1).

Open a gap in the whole song (R-ARR-2), ONE edit: every clip, automation point, marker and the loop at or after --at moves --length beats later; a section, a looping automation's span or the loop that holds --at grows by it. A clip that starts before --at and crosses it stays (it is named — split it to open the gap through it, R-EDIT-1). The loop is the session's: undo leaves it.

Take a span out of the whole song (R-ARR-2), ONE edit: what lies wholly inside it goes (clips, automation points, markers), what follows moves earlier by its length; a section, a looping span or the loop that crosses it shrinks. A clip that repeats its material (a note clip, an audio clip set to loop) and starts before --from is shortened by the overlap; any other clip crossing --from or --to is refused, naming it — split it first (R-EDIT-1) or move it.

Lock a pattern to a scale (R-ROLL-11) — `pattern scale pt_1 D dorian`: a note placed (`note add`, its --chord, `notes add`) lands on the scale's nearest pitch, a tie going down (so a major chord stamped on any degree is that degree's own triad); a note moved in pitch (`note move --to-pitch`, `notes move --semi`) goes on to the scale's next pitch the way it moved. A move in time, an import, a step row, a recording and `pattern transpose` keep their pitches; notes already written stay. `off` unlocks it. The scales are under Notation. Prints its notes.
Set several notes' --vel, --chance and/or --length as ONE edit — the piano roll's selection. Refused whole, naming the first, when a name matches no note.

Loosen the notes (R-ROLL-11): each start moved within ± --timing beats and each velocity within ± --vel (with neither: 0.02 and 8), a triangular spread from a seed — the same --seed on the same notes writes the same notes (by default a hash of the notes; printed). A note never goes before beat 0, nor onto another of its pitch (it keeps its time). --notes: only those notes (the roll's selection).

End every note where the next start begins — a chord's notes together, the last at the pattern's end; an overlap is shortened as a gap is filled (R-ROLL-11). --notes: only those notes, the next start among them.

A MIDI effect written as notes (R-ROLL-11): on every --rate step of the beat grid (0.25) where notes are held, the next pitch of what is held there — its pitches over --octaves (1), up, down, updown (the turns not repeated) or a seeded random (--seed) — --gate of a step long (1), at the held note's velocity and chance; it starts again from the first after a rest. Replaces the notes it arpeggiated (every note, or --notes); a step on another note of its pitch replaces that one. Prints how many.

Make patterns of a Standard MIDI File (format 0/1/2; ticks or SMPTE time): one per track with notes, or --track n's alone; whole bars long; named after the track. With --lane <an instrument's track> or --instrument <type>: ONE pattern (every track merged, or --track's) and a clip of it at --at, by `clip add`'s rules — what dropping a .mid does. Prints the (first) pattern; `made:` the rest.
Write a pattern as a MIDI file (format 1, 960 ticks a beat — Solaris's own, so it imports back exact; channel 10 when a kit plays it).
Write the song's notes as a MIDI file: a track per instrument strip, every note clip's pattern where the clip plays it (repeated to fill it), the song's tempo and meter.
Move every note by --semi semitones (negative = down). Refused if a note would leave 0–127.
Its notes, one per line in the `notes add` notation (pitch as a name or pad), the number after `#`.

Automate a number: a new automation named "<owner> · <parameter>", ranged as it, holding its value from beat 0 to the song's end, shown on the timeline — and the address bound to `=au_n`. Prints the id. --pump: already LOOPING every beat (R-AUTO-13) — down on the beat (18 dB for a level, else to 20 % of its range), back to its value by the middle of the beat: the side-chain feel. Loop any automation with `set <au>.loop=<beats>` (`.at`, `.length`: where it repeats, R-AUTO-12).
An automation from nothing (default range 0…1). It moves nothing until a formula reads it. Prints the id.
Delete an automation. Refused while a formula reads it, unless --unbind (those bindings are cleared).
Add a point (one at the same beat is replaced). Its shape governs the segment after it (a bezier point's handles start flat: speed 0, influence 33.333 %).
Move the point at --at to another beat and/or value.
Remove the point at --at.

Set how the curve leaves the point at --at. A BEZIER point is Interstellar's key (R-ANIM-2): on each side a speed — the slope there, in the automation's unit per beat — and an influence, how far into the neighbouring segment it pulls (0 < x ≤ 100 %); flags not given are kept. One line per handle gesture.
Clear an address's formula: it plays its own stored value again. (`set <address>=<number>` clears and sets.)
The value an address plays at a beat (default 0); --explain shows its formula and every name it reads.

Render offline: the master to --out; with --stems, each named strip's (`all`: every strip's) post-fader output to <out>.<ch>.<ext>; with --ports, each output port to <out>.<port>.<ext>. The tail runs until −90 dBFS or 10 s. Every file starts at --from exactly: the latency of a lookahead device (a limiter) is compensated and trimmed (R-MIX-17). The format is the extension — .wav, .flac, .mp3, .ogg (Vorbis), .opus — or --format (R-EXPORT-1). --rate renders the song AT that rate (Opus: 48000, its default; MP3 to 48000); --bits 16 | 24 (WAV and FLAC; default 24) | 32f (WAV) — 16 and 24 TPDF-dithered; --kbps for the lossy ones (MP3 32…320, default 320; Ogg 45…500, 256; Opus 6…510, 192). --normalize gains every file alike to that integrated loudness, held so the master's true peak stays under --ceiling (dBTP, default −1) — said on a `normalize` line. --measure prints the written master's integrated loudness, the most of its momentary and short-term, its true peak and its lowest correlation (R-METER-1).
Every route and send at once: rows = strips, columns = destinations.
The mix report: unused strips, clips on muted strips, unreachable strips, single-input buses, offline media, unknown devices, clipping.

The whole AppModel; --stable omits what changes with time. --json --compact: the SONG only (no registry, machine, recents or browser), on one line; a device lists only its non-default parameters as `name=value`, a pattern its notes in the `notes add` notation.
The song as a tree of ids and names: mixers → strips (kind, devices, output, sends), the master, lanes → clips (at, length, pattern or file), patterns (length, notes, clips), automations.
One node's fields that differ from their defaults; a device's non-default parameters with their units (and the default); `show project` for the song.
This document: every command, event, model field and device parameter.

The MACHINE's settings (never a song's): sampleRate (new songs, and the clock device's rate), bufferSize (frames), output / input (device ids from `devices list`; empty = the system default), port.<name>=<device>:<channel> (where a song's port plays on this machine), metronome (on|off), metronomeLevel (dB), auditionLevel (dB, the browser's preview), newBpm / newSig (what a new song starts at), reducedMotion (on|off), showIds (on|off: every object's id beside its name, R-UI-11), autosave (seconds between autosaves of an unsaved song, or off — R-SAFE-1), key.<action>=<combos> (R-SET-4: a keyboard action's keys — a comma list such as "Ctrl+Shift+Z, Ctrl+Y", `none`, or `default`; a combo another action of the same keyboard has is refused naming it — the actions are in this document's Keyboard section). Saved at once.
The machine's settings.
Add a sample folder to the browser's quick-access list.
Remove a sample folder from the list (the folder itself is untouched).
Reorder the sample folders.
List this machine's audio devices (ids for `settings set output=…`).

List a folder for the browser: sub-folders, audio files, songs. --search <text> (R-PRESET-3): the audio files whose name holds it or that carry a tag starting with it — in the sample folders (or <folder>) eight levels down, the first 200, and the library's tagged files; --favourites: the favourites.
Tag a sound in the machine's library (R-PRESET-3): a word of letters, digits or dashes, kept in lower case. No undo.
Take a tag off a sound (R-PRESET-3).
Mark a sound a favourite, or not (R-PRESET-3; on when not said).

Find the VST3 plugins where this machine keeps them (R-VST-6: SOLARIS_VST3_PATH, else ~/.vst3, /usr/lib/vst3, /usr/local/lib/vst3) — each bundle read in a process of its own, so one that crashes loses only itself (said). Prints each found and each problem; the list is the machine's, kept.
The VST3 plugins the last scan found (R-VST-6).
Start a plugin device's process again — after a crash or an overrun took it offline — from its last state (R-VST-6). Not an edit. Prints `playing`, or `offline: <why>`.

Bind a MIDI control — `<n>` (0–127, on any channel) or `<ch>/<n>` (on channel 1–16) — to a number a formula can drive (R-CTRL-1): moved, it sets it over its travel (a gain by the fader law, a device parameter by its taper). One address per control. The machine's setting (`map.<cc>` in its file), not an edit.
Forget a MIDI control's mapping (R-CTRL-1).
Every MIDI mapping: `<cc> <address>`, `(inert)` where the open song has no such address (R-CTRL-1).
Wait for the next MIDI control moved and bind it — on its channel — to <address> (said: `map.learned`; its value is not taken); --cancel stops waiting (R-CTRL-1).

Open a plugin device's OWN editor in a window of its own — the plugin's process makes it (R-VST-6) — or, with --close, close it. What is turned there reaches the song as `set <dv>.p<id>`. Not an edit. Prints `open` or `closed`.
Take a song off Home's recent list (the file is untouched).

Play on the clock device (settings output), from --from or where the transport stands. Edits while playing are heard: a gain, a pan, a mute, a solo, a device parameter at once; anything structural by a new engine swapped in at the same position. --clip plays that clip's span looped, the whole song sounding there (the piano roll's play, R-ROLL-6): it follows the clip as it is edited, and the song's own loop comes back at `transport stop`, a plain `transport play` or a `transport loop`.

Stop; the transport stays where it was heard — or, with --return, goes back to the cue: where the time bar was last put (a seek, or a play's --from or --clip; `transport.cue`). A plain stop's place is temporary: the next play starts there but the cue stays.
Move the transport (playing or not) — to a beat, or to a marker (R-ARR-1).
This machine's MIDI inputs (ALSA sequencer ports), each marked when Solaris listens to it — the names `settings set midiInputs=` takes.
Clear the meters: every clip light and held peak, and the master's true peak and integrated loudness start again (the song is not edited; a click on a clip light).

Play and record the armed strip's keyboard (R-MIDI-2): at `transport stop` what was played becomes a new note clip on its track from the bar it began in — or, with --overdub, notes added to the strip's clip under the start — each note where it was HEARD, its start on the `recordQuantize` grid; one undo takes it back. --count-in (else `settings countIn`) bars of click first, the song waiting. With an AUDIO line armed (R-REC-1): its input from where recording begins to the stop, written beside the song (`Recordings/<strip> <n>.wav`) and put on the strip as a clip where it began — moved earlier by the output's and the input's latency, kept only inside `transport punch` — one undo.

Choose which take plays where (R-REC-2): take <n> (1-based) from --from to --to (song beats; the whole clip without them) — ONE edit, the range overwriting what it covers. Where no range says, the last take plays; the seams are crossfaded 5 ms. A loop recording makes the takes.

Cut an audio clip in two at --at (song beats, inside it) — ONE edit (R-EDIT-1): the first half keeps the id and the fade in, the second (printed) begins at --at with the fade out; together they play what the one did. A reversed clip's first half is its span's end; a clip with takes keeps them all, its comp divided. A looping clip is cut only where a repetition begins; a note clip not at all (its notes are its pattern's).

Join audio clips of one strip into ONE (R-EDIT-1): what they play — gain, fades, crossfades, reverse, comps — rendered raw (before the strip's devices, fader and pan) from the first's start to the last's end, written beside the song as Bounces/<strip> <n>.wav (32-bit float) and put in their place on the first's lane; one edit, the new clip printed. A note clip is refused (a strip's bounce is R-PERF-3).

Cut an audio clip into clips (R-EDIT-1): --every <beats> from its start, or --transients where a sound begins (the DSP library's onset detector, REQ-onset-1; --sensitivity 0 … 1, 0.5) — ONE edit, the clips printed. --every with --kit makes a new instrument track instead: a Sampler of the clip's file in N equal slices (mode=slices) and a note clip in the clip's place playing them in order (root + k for slice k), so it plays what the clip did; the clip stays. A looping clip is not sliced.
Punch in and out (R-REC-1): a recording keeps only what the song plays from <from> to <to> beats, and its clip starts at <from>; `off` keeps it all. The session's, as the loop.
Loop between two beats while playing — or a marker's section (R-ARR-1: its length, else to the next marker); `off` ends it.
Hear a sample now, outside the song (the browser's preview): through the output device at the audition level, to its end; `stop` ends it. Not an edit, never in a render.
Let time pass (playback goes on, the model's transport and meters update) — for scripts that listen.

events.name: info
events.summary: A note worth logging; carries no state.

events.name: error
events.summary: Something failed. Also set as AppModel.lastError.

events.name: command.rejected
events.summary: A line was refused (R-SVC-3): unknown verb, flag, address or parameter; a refused edit.

events.name: screen.changed
events.summary: home | project.

events.name: project.opened
events.summary: A song is open.

events.name: project.saved
events.summary: The .slp was written.

events.name: project.closed
events.summary: Back to Home.

events.name: project.changed
events.summary: A node was added, removed, moved or re-routed. what = e.g. strip.added, clip.moved, route.set. Every node a command makes is announced, one event each (R-SVC-8).

events.name: params.changed
events.summary: An address was written; value is what was STORED, canonical (a value out of range is refused, never clamped — R-SVC-8).

events.name: render.finished
events.summary: A render was written; peak is the master's, dBFS.

events.name: render.failed
events.summary: A render stopped with an error.

events.name: audit.report
events.summary: How many findings `audit` printed.

events.name: settings.changed
events.summary: A machine setting changed and was saved: sampleRate, bufferSize, output, input, port.<name>, folders, key.<action> (R-SET-4) …

events.name: devices.changed
events.summary: `devices list` found this many devices.

events.name: browse.changed
events.summary: The browser now lists this folder — or, a search (path `search:<text>` / `favourites`), what it found.

events.name: library.changed
events.summary: R-PRESET-3: a file's tags (favourite among them) changed and were saved; tags comma-separated, '' none.

events.name: plugins.changed
events.summary: R-VST-6: a scan found this many plugins; problems: bundles that could not be read.

events.name: plugin.offline
events.summary: R-VST-6: a song's plugin is not playing — it never started, crashed or overran its budget; an effect passes dry, an instrument is silent (`device reload <dv>`). Said once.

events.name: surface.changed
events.summary: R-CTRL-2: the control surface connected (1) or not (0, why), or moved to another bank of eight.

events.name: map.learned
events.summary: R-CTRL-1: the MIDI control moved during a `map learn` is bound to the address (on its channel: `<ch>/<n>`).

events.name: plugin.editor
events.summary: R-VST-6: a plugin's own editor window opened (1) or closed (0) — by `device editor`, or its window's own close.

events.name: recents.changed
events.summary: Home's recent songs changed.

events.name: transport.changed
events.summary: Play, stop, seek or loop: playing 1/0, position in beats, loop `from-to` or `off`.

events.name: audition.changed
events.summary: A sample previewed from the browser started (playing 1) or ended — stopped, or to its end (playing 0).

events.name: note.previewed
events.summary: A note was heard through a strip, outside the song (`note preview`, the piano roll's sound — R-ROLL-7).

events.name: project.autosaved
events.summary: The unsaved song was written beside it (`<song>.autosave`, R-SAFE-1).

events.name: project.recovery
events.summary: The song just opened has an autosave newer than it (age in seconds) — `project recover` restores it, `project discard-recovery` drops it (R-SAFE-2).

events.name: record.finished
events.summary: A recording landed: its notes in this clip ('' — nothing was played) (R-MIDI-2); an audio take, how long it is (R-REC-1); how many takes a looped recording made (R-REC-2).

events.name: strip.armed
events.summary: The MIDI keyboard plays this strip now ('' — none); the session's, not the song's (R-MIDI-2).

events.name: meters.cleared
events.summary: The clip lights and held peaks are out; the master's true peak and integrated loudness start again (R-METER-2).

devices.label: Basic Synth
devices.summary: Two oscillators and noise through a resonant filter and an amplitude envelope; 16 voices.

devices.label: Wavetable
devices.summary: Two wavetable oscillators — six built-in tables, or a sound of 2048-point cycles — moved through by a position and the filter envelope; band-limited at every pitch; a resonant filter, two envelopes; 16 voices.

devices.label: FM Synth
devices.summary: Four sine operators by phase modulation — eight algorithms, operator 4 fed back, an envelope each; 16 voices.

devices.label: Piano
devices.summary: A physical piano: felt hammers on stiff, inharmonic strings through a shared bridge and soundboard; sustain and soft pedals; 16 voices, a held key never stolen while a released one rings.

devices.label: Drum Machine
devices.summary: Twelve synthesized pads on the GM drum notes (36 kick … 56 cowbell, a crash 49 and a ride 51); the closed hat chokes the open hat.
A tuned bass drum: the note's pitch punched down to at each attack, gliding between held notes; a long decay, a click, drive and a tone; one voice.

devices.label: Granular
devices.summary: A recorded sound as a cloud of short grains — their size, density and place (scanned, sprayed), pitched by the note, sprayed in pitch and pan; an envelope; 16 voices.

devices.label: Multi-sample
devices.summary: A recorded instrument read from an SFZ file: its sounds by key and velocity, in turn (round robin) or by chance, looped or one-shot, choking each other; an envelope each; 32 voices.

devices.label: Sampler
devices.summary: Plays a recorded sound: pitched by the note (chromatic), as recorded (one-shot), or as a kit of its span's equal slices (slices); a span, reverse, an ADSR.

devices.label: Compressor
devices.summary: Feed-forward peak compressor; with Sidechain on it listens to another track (its key).

devices.label: EQ
devices.summary: Low cut, low shelf, three peaks, high shelf, high cut.

devices.label: Gate
devices.summary: A gate and a downward expander: below its threshold turned down by the ratio, held open before it closes; keyed by another track if asked.

devices.label: Convolution Reverb
devices.summary: A recorded room: an impulse response (a sample) convolved with the sound, its latency reported.

devices.label: Imager
devices.summary: Wider or narrower, and mono below a frequency: mid and side, the side scaled, its lows taken away.

devices.label: Flanger
devices.summary: A short delay swept by an LFO and fed back: a comb whose teeth sweep.

devices.label: Phaser
devices.summary: Notches swept by an LFO: first-order all-passes fed back, mixed with the dry sound.

devices.label: Saturator
devices.summary: A curve driven — soft, hard, tube or fold — four times oversampled, its latency reported.

devices.label: Bitcrusher
devices.summary: Fewer bits and a lower rate: each sample rounded to a coarser grid, held for longer.

devices.label: De-esser
devices.summary: Sibilance held down: a high-pass hears it, its level held at the threshold — the band alone turned down (split) or the whole sound (wide).

devices.label: Transient Shaper
devices.summary: More or less attack, more or less sustain, whatever the level: a fast envelope against two slow ones.

devices.label: Multiband
devices.summary: Three bands split by Linkwitz-Riley crossovers, each compressed alone; flat when nothing is.

devices.label: Reverb
devices.summary: Feedback-delay-network reverb, decorrelated stereo.

devices.label: Delay
devices.summary: Feedback echo, each repeat darker.

devices.label: Chorus
devices.summary: LFO-modulated short delay.

devices.label: Drive
devices.summary: tanh waveshaper with a tone low-pass.

devices.label: Filter
devices.summary: The synth's resonant state-variable filter, with a dry/wet mix.

devices.label: Limiter
devices.summary: Brickwall lookahead limiter: the output never exceeds the ceiling.
